title: Media jobs finish late
briefing: Processing latency has increased for media jobs. Inspect processing progress and recent worker signals.

actions.label: Inspect media worker restarts
actions.criteria: Use when jobs stop during processing or restart counts rise without a known cause.
actions.instructions: Compare worker start times, process exit reasons, and job progress markers.

actions.label: Compare decoded image memory
actions.criteria: Use when affected image dimensions or frame counts plausibly exceed the worker memory budget.
actions.instructions: Estimate decoded pixels and bytes per frame for affected jobs, then compare with the worker memory limit.

actions.label: Inspect object storage download latency
actions.criteria: Use when worker delays occur while fetching input objects.
actions.instructions: Compare download latency and response errors for affected and healthy objects.

fallback: Collect a job ID, its last processing stage, and one worker lifecycle event for that job.

events.text: Media job completion latency exceeded 120 seconds. No stage breakdown is attached.
Three media workers restarted while processing jobs from class M38. Inputs were fetched successfully before all three restarts. Exit reasons have not arrived.
Class M38 image workers have a 384 MiB memory limit. The decoder holds the uncompressed four-channel image in memory during conversion.
Input metadata sampled for class M38: 12000 by 12000 pixels, four channels, one byte per channel.

debrief.summary: Class M38 included inputs whose decoded pixel buffer alone exceeded the worker memory limit. The orchestrator later confirmed memory-limit termination.
lessons: Compressed object size is a poor proxy for decoding memory.
Compare decoded dimensions with the memory budget for the affected worker class.
